This is a claim petition U/s 166 read with Section 140 of The Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988 ( Old Act)
filed by petitioners.

2. Coming to the facts of the case, it is stated that on 06.07.2014, at about 10:20 am, Ram Kumar (
deceased) was going to Najafgarh for purchasing some goods on his bicycle alongwith his cousin Chattarpati, who was on his bicycle.

When they reached near Metro Hospital, Chawla Stand Najafgarh suddenly, a truck bearing No. DL1GB5197 being driven by respondent No.1 at a very high speed, rashly and negligently without taking necessary precautions and violating the traffic rules came from behind and hit bicycle of deceased Ram Kumar.
Due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
The injured was taken to Metro Hospital where he was declared brought dead.
The present case pertains to the death of Ram Kumar.
3. Contending that the said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving of Truck bearing no DL1GB 5197 by Constable Sudhir, Shahi MACT No.380/16
Gauri Shanker & Ors.
Vs. Sudhir Shahi & Ors.
Page No. 6 of 12 (respondent no. 1).
He has been made as R.1.

The offending truck was owned by Delhi Police, (respondent no. 2) The petitioners have filed the present claim thereby claiming a sum of Rs. 7,50,000/ (Seven lacs and Fifty Thousand) from respondents as compensation, alongwith interest @ 18% from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
4.
The respondent no.1 has filed his written statement stating therein that no accident had taken place from the vehicle of the respondent No.1 and a false case has been registered against him.
5. The respondent no. 2 has not filed any W.S on its behalf.

6. After completion of the proceedings, following issues were framed on 12.10.2015:
(i)

Whether Ram Kumar S/O Gauri Shankar sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 06.07.2014 due to rash and negligent driving of of vehicle (Truck) bearing no. DL1GB 5197 being driven by Respondent No.1 and owner by Respondent No.2?

DL1GB 5197 being driven by Respondent No.1 and owner by Respondent No.2? OPP 9.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
To prove this issue, petitioners examined eye witness, PW2 Chhaarpati.
Who has deposed that that on 06.07.2014 at about 10:20 am, he alongwith his cousin Ram Kumar were going from their house to Chhawla stand to purchase some goods for mason work .
He has deposed that they were on their separate bicycle.

When they reached near Metro Hospital, Chawla Stand Najafgarh suddenly, a truck bearing No. DL1GB5197 being driven by respondent No.1 at a very high speed, rashly and negligently, violating the traffic rules came from behind and hit bicycle of deceased Ram Kumar.
Due to which he fell down on the road and sustained severe injuries.
He has deposed that injured was taken to Metro Hospital where he was declared brought dead by the Doctor.
PW 2 has not been crossexamined by respondent No.1 and 2, so the testimony of PW2 with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 remains unrebutted.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/304A of IPC.

Though,
respondent no.1 has examined himself as RW1 and denied the factum of accident with the offending vehicle.
The fact that Ram Kumar died in that accident is also supported by his postmortem report on the dead body of victim.

10. So considering the testimony of PW 2 and charge sheet against R1, this Tribunal is not accepting the testimony of R1W1 to the extent that he MACT No.380/16 Gauri Shanker & Ors. Vs.
Sudhir Shahi & Ors.

sentences.text: Page No. 8 of 12 has not caused any accident.
But after investigation, police indicted respondent no.1 for offences punishable under Sections 279/304A of IPC.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1, who is also a police official and R.1 has not filed any complaint against the police officer to any higher authority against his such implication.

Rather considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of Truck bearing No.DL1 GB 5197 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Ram Kumar.

11. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Ram Kumar died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of Truck bearing no DL1GB 5197 by respondent no.1.

sentences.text: It is not disputed during arguments that petitioners are the mother and father of victim.
Moreover, this fact is established by statement of Sh Gauri Shankar (PW1) father of deceased.
Being LRs of deceased, petitioners are well within their rights to claim compensation from respondents.
13. Now coming to the extent of compensation.
It is deposed by PW1 in his evidence affidavit that at the time of accident, deceased was less than 12 years of age.
As per marksheet of Municipal Corporation of Delhi, school of the deceased, his date of birth was 12.10.2002.

The Schedule II annexed with Section 163A of The Motor Vehicles Act, provides for notional income of minor , as Rs.15,000/ p.a for computation of compensation in MACT No.380/16 Gauri Shanker & Ors. Vs.
Sudhir Shahi & Ors. Page No. 9 of 12 case of death of minor in motor transport accident.

sentences.text: But due to lapse of lot of time, this provision has become inadequate.

Th Hon'ble High Court of Delhi,while disposing of 16 appeals through a single judgment titled as Chetan Malhotra Vs. Lala Ram etc. MAC APP. No. 554/2010 etc. decided on 13.05.2016, envisaged a formula called as "inflation correction method", taking financial year of 199798 as base year for computaion of compensation.

entities.text: Chetan Malhotra Vs. Lala Ram etc. MAC APP. No. 554/2010 etc
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation has to be computed as per formula ie Rs. 15,000 x A / 331.

Figure of Rs. 15,000/
represents the notional income, specified in Second Schedule.
'A' represents CII for the financial year, in which victim died and figure 331 represents the CII for the base year.
14. In the present case accident in question was occurred on 06.07.2014.

Therefore, CII of Rs.
1024/ for the financial year 20142015 would apply.
Counting in this way, notional income of victim comes to 15000 x 1024 / 331 = 46,404/, rounded off to 47,000/.

After deduction towards personal and living expenses and applying the multiplier of 15 as the age of the deceased was 12 years, the total pecuniary loss to estate is calculated as 47000/ x 2/3 x 15 = 4,70,000/.

The Similar amount of Rs. 4,70,000/ is also granted to petitioners as nonpecuniary damages,
including future prospects of victim, making a total sum of Rs. 9,40,000/.
The interest @ 7.5% per annum is awarded on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till the date of compliance.
15. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondents No.1 and No.2 by holding that they are jointly and serverally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is a claim petition U/s 166 read with Section 140 of The Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988 ( Old Act)
filed by petitioners.
2. Coming to the facts of the case, it is stated that on 06.07.2014, at about 10:20 am, Ram Kumar (
deceased) was going to Najafgarh for purchasing some goods on his bicycle alongwith his cousin Chattarpati, who was on his bicycle.
When they reached near Metro Hospital, Chawla Stand Najafgarh suddenly, a truck bearing No. DL1GB5197 being driven by respondent No.1 at a very high speed, rashly and negligently without taking necessary precautions and violating the traffic rules came from behind and hit bicycle of deceased Ram Kumar.
Due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
The injured was taken to Metro Hospital where he was declared brought dead.
Due to which he fell down on the road and sustained severe injuries.
PW 2 has not been crossexamined by respondent No.1 and 2, so the testimony of PW2 with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 remains unrebutted.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/304A of IPC.
Though,
respondent no.1 has examined himself as RW1 and denied the factum of accident with the offending vehicle.
The fact that Ram Kumar died in that accident is also supported by his postmortem report on the dead body of victim.
10. So considering the testimony of PW 2 and charge sheet against R1, this Tribunal is not accepting the testimony of R1W1 to the extent that he MACT No.380/16 Gauri Shanker & Ors. Vs.
Sudhir Shahi & Ors.
Page No. 8 of 12 has not caused any accident.
But after investigation, police indicted respondent no.1 for offences punishable under Sections 279/304A of IPC.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1, who is also a police official and R.1 has not filed any complaint against the police officer to any higher authority against his such implication.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether Ram Kumar S/O Gauri Shankar sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated 06.07.2014 due to rash and negligent driving of of vehicle (Truck) bearing no. DL1GB 5197 being driven by Respondent No.1 and owner by Respondent No.2?
OPP (ii) Whether petitioners are entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?
11. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Ram Kumar died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash and negligent driving of Truck bearing no DL1GB 5197 by respondent no.1.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Rather considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of Truck bearing No.DL1 GB 5197 by respondent no.1 thereby causing death of Ram Kumar.
Being LRs of deceased, petitioners are well within their rights to claim compensation from respondents.
The Schedule II annexed with Section 163A of The Motor Vehicles Act, provides for notional income of minor , as Rs.15,000/ p.a for computation of compensation in MACT No.380/16 Gauri Shanker & Ors. Vs.
Sudhir Shahi & Ors. Page No. 9 of 12 case of death of minor in motor transport accident.
